title: Superhero Flying Game
subtitle: A 2D superhero flying game built in Unity, combining aerial movement, collectible items, projectile combat, and evolving boss attack systems.
overview: A 2D superhero flying game developed in Unity, originally created as a university group project exploring an augmented reality (AR)-inspired gaming experience for an in-car environment. The game simulated an AR display by overlaying gameplay onto video footage filmed from a car window, creating the impression that the superhero was flying through the surrounding environment. I have since returned to the project independently to review the existing implementation, improve the code structure, refine gameplay systems, and build on the original prototype.

team.size: Originally a university group project; now independently developed
team.about: The project brought together a multidisciplinary team, with each member contributing to a different aspect of development. I worked closely with the designer to shape the core gameplay. I exposed configurable variables in the Unity Inspector, allowing the designer to adjust gameplay values and help fine-tune the experience through iteration. Temporary assets were used during early development while the visual direction was established. Once the art direction was finalised, the artists created the visual assets and 3D models, which I imported and integrated into the game environment. The psychology team member focused on ensuring the game was appropriate for its intended audience. This included evaluating the experience against the target audience's needs and conducting playtesting sessions to gather feedback on how the game was received.

audience: Originally aimed at children, the game is now intended to appeal to players of all ages.

objectives.title: Engaging Gameplay
objectives.description: Create a fun and engaging flying game that meets the project brief, combining movement, dodging incoming attacks, and firing at boss enemies to keep players actively involved.

objectives.title: Gameplay Variety
objectives.description: Introduce unique power-ups and abilities to add variety to gameplay, giving players exciting features to discover and use.

objectives.title: Rewards and Challenge
objectives.description: Reward players with points for collecting coins while navigating hazards and avoiding enemy attacks, balancing risk and reward.

objectives.title: AR-Inspired Experience
objectives.description: Simulate an augmented reality-inspired experience by overlaying gameplay onto footage filmed from a car window, creating the impression of flying through the surrounding environment.

decisions.title: Unity and C#
decisions.description: Use Unity as the development engine and C# to implement gameplay logic, player interactions, movement, and other game systems.

decisions.title: Configurable Gameplay Parameters
decisions.description: Expose gameplay variables in the Unity Inspector so values could be adjusted without repeatedly modifying the underlying code. This supported collaboration with the designer and made it easier to fine-tune the gameplay through iteration.

decisions.title: Procedural World Generation
decisions.description: Procedurally generate and place game objects, including platforms, clouds, and power-ups, in the direction the player is travelling. This helps create a continuously evolving environment as the player flies through the game world.

decisions.title: Asset Integration Workflow
decisions.description: Use temporary assets during early development while the visual direction was being established. Integrate the final artwork and 3D models once the art direction had been agreed upon, allowing gameplay development to progress alongside the art process.

decisions.title: Leap Motion Gesture Controls
decisions.description: Leap Motion was introduced as an additional feature proposed by the designer, outside the original project scope. I assessed its technical feasibility and implemented hand gesture-based movement controls, allowing players to control the superhero's movement through physical gestures rather than relying solely on conventional input methods.

decisions.title: AR-Inspired Presentation
decisions.description: Overlay gameplay onto video footage filmed from a car window to simulate an augmented reality-inspired in-car experience without relying on live AR tracking.

challenges.title: Project Scope and Time Management
challenges.problem: As a university team, we needed to agree on a game concept that could be delivered within the project deadline while balancing other coursework. With several gameplay ideas to consider, we had to decide which features were essential to the core experience and which were realistic to implement within the available time.
challenges.solution: We evaluated our ideas based on their complexity and contribution to the gameplay, prioritising the core mechanics before considering additional features. This helped us establish a manageable scope and focus development effort on delivering the essential experience.

challenges.title: Gameplay Balancing and Iteration
challenges.problem: The game's movement, platform behaviour, scaling, and procedural object placement all influenced the overall gameplay experience. Finding suitable values required testing and collaboration with the designer to refine how the game played.
challenges.solution: I exposed configurable gameplay variables in the Unity Inspector so the designer could adjust values and provide feedback without requiring changes to the underlying code. This made it easier to experiment with different settings and refine the gameplay through iteration.

challenges.title: Leap Motion SDK Integration
challenges.problem: The designer proposed Leap Motion as an additional feature beyond the original project scope. I needed to establish whether the SDK could be integrated into the existing game and whether hand gestures could provide a practical alternative to conventional movement controls.
challenges.solution: I investigated the SDK and integrated it into the project, first establishing basic gesture-based movement before extending the implementation to support more advanced gestures. This allowed me to assess the feasibility of the feature and expand the game's control options.

challenges.title: Revisiting and Modernising the Original Project
challenges.problem: Returning to the project independently years later gave me the opportunity to reassess the original implementation and identify areas for improvement, while preserving the concept and gameplay that defined the prototype.
challenges.solution: I began reviewing and restructuring the existing code, refining gameplay systems, and building on the original implementation. My aim is to make the project easier to maintain and extend while retaining its core superhero flying concept and AR-inspired presentation.

outcome: The project resulted in a playable 2D superhero flying game developed in Unity, featuring player movement, procedurally generated platforms and objects, collectibles, enemy encounters, and an AR-inspired presentation using footage filmed from a car window. Returning to the project independently has allowed me to build on that foundation, review the existing implementation, and continue refining the gameplay and code structure.
learnings: Developing this project strengthened my understanding of gameplay programming in Unity and C#, particularly in procedural generation, configurable gameplay systems, and integrating alternative input methods through the Leap Motion SDK. Working with a multidisciplinary team also taught me the importance of collaboration and designing flexible systems that support iteration. Revisiting the project years later has reinforced the value of maintainable code and shown me how an existing prototype can be reviewed, improved, and extended beyond its original scope.
